brief: Goldman Sachs cross-asset weekly. August nonfarm payrolls rose 162k, prior employment growth was revised higher and unemployment held at 4.1%, an upside surprise that raised market expectations of a September Fed hike despite White House calls for lower rates. This week's focus is US PPI and CPI plus central bank decisions including the ECB. The procyclical rotation since June 30 continued on higher nominal growth but slowed. Commodities led, driven by European gas and refined products on SoH tensions, with grains also among the largest moves. Equity benchmarks stayed range-bound while leadership shifted, as one of the sharpest momentum factor unwinds broadened returns into non-Tech and defensives, Energy first and Financials and Health Care the strongest non-energy sectors. Sovereign bonds sold off toward post-GFC yield highs led by real yields, which GS attributes to strong nominal growth, fiscal concerns and crowding out from AI-related debt issuance. Gold rallied despite higher US real yields, tied to safe-haven demand after US Treasury interventions in the yen and long-dated Treasuries. GS stays tactically Neutral over 3 months and modestly pro-risk over 12 months: OW equities, N bonds, N commodities, N cash, UW credit, with AI exposure combined with high-dividend and low-volatility styles.
